Class GridColumn

java.lang.Object
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.GridColumn
public final class GridColumn extends Object

One column of a Grid, addressed by its model index: its width and the limits for it, visibility, renderer and header. Get it with Grid.getColumn(int); setters return the column, so settings chain:

grid.getColumn(0).setWidth(80).setMaxWidth(120);
grid.getColumn(2).setRenderer(CellRenderers.number("#,##0.00")).setMinWidth(90)
        .setHeaderStyle(CellStyle.DEFAULT.withAlignment(HPos.RIGHT));

A column object belongs to the model the grid showed when it was taken; once the grid shows another model, or the model no longer has the column, its methods throw IllegalStateException. It holds no state of its own: two objects for the same column of the same model are equal.

    • setComparator

      public GridColumn setComparator(Comparator<?> comparator)

      Sorts this column with its own order instead of the default (numbers by value, text ignoring case, other values by their natural order); null goes back to the default. Nulls come first in ascending order and last in descending order, and the comparator never sees them. If the grid is sorted by this column, it sorts again.

      grid.getColumn("Name").setComparator(Collator.getInstance(Locale.GERMAN));
      Parameters:
      comparator - the order for the column's non-null values, or null
      Returns:
      this column

    • setConverter

      public GridColumn setConverter(javafx.util.StringConverter<?> converter)
      Converts between values and text for editing this column in place: toString fills the editor, fromString reads what was typed, and an exception from it marks the input invalid. Without one, the grid edits text, numbers in the default locale's format or plain, booleans, enum constants by name, and ISO or localized dates and times; other types are not edited.
      Parameters:
      converter - the converter, or null for the built-in one
      Returns:
      this column
